speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old female at 30 weeks gestation. The patient presents with a sudden onset of fever, headache, anorexia, fatigue, and malaise. She reports the consumption of ice cream 3 days prior to the onset of symptoms.

speaker: Doctor

Thank you for the details. The sudden onset of fever and headache following ice cream consumption at 30 weeks gestation raises concern for Listeria monocytogenes infection. Can you tell me if you have noticed any muscle aches or if your symptoms have worsened over the last 48 hours?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Listeria monocytogenes infection (Listeriosis).

The blood culture results showing Gram-positive rods with tumbling motility are pathognomonic for Listeria. Given your pregnancy, these findings indicate an invasive listeriosis which requires immediate intravenous antibiotic treatment.
